title: Take one tissue from a pop-up box and leave the next one standing ready
instruction: Take one tissue out of the box and put it on the tray, leaving the box in place with the next tissue ready to pull.
context: Pulling one tissue from a pop-up box is something nearly everyone has done. Pop-up tissues are interfolded: the film slit squeezes the sheet you pull against the next one, so friction drags the next one's edge up after it and the film then holds it standing, ready for the next pull. Doing it well takes care. Grab both sheets and the next one comes out too. Pinch the thin sheet once and pull, and it can creep out of the fingers and fall back into the box, so it is pulled hand over hand. The same squeeze also drags on the box, which is light near its last sheets, and people often steady it with the other hand. At the end the pulled tissue lies where it was passed, the box is where it stood and the next tissue stands ready in the slit. Both tissues are cloth soft bodies and the film edge a light sprung strip; the coupling, the hold and the box's motion all come from contact friction, with no scripted rule.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), everything square to the table. A flat pop-up tissue box at full size (Kleenex Professional flat box 21400: 22.5 x 12.1 x 5.1 cm, printed paperboard) lies free on the table, long axis along x, centred at x 23, y -6. Centred in its top is the usual oval opening (8.9 x 5.7 cm, long axis along x) covered by clear polyethylene film with one slit (8.3 cm) along the long axis. One film edge of the slit is fixed; the other is pressed against the sheets (about 0.14 N). Inside, a light foam spacer block fills the box to 2 cm under the lid, and on it lie the last two sheets; box, spacer and sheets weigh 40 g. The sheets are pale pink 2-ply facial tissues cut down to 7 x 7.8 cm (top) and 7 x 6.1 cm (next) and interfolded by hand: the top one stands 2.5 cm up out of the slit; inside, it bends round the leading edge of the next one and lies under it; the next one's edge waits just inside the slit. A grey moulded polypropylene tray (15 x 12 cm inside, 1.2 cm rim, fixed) is at x 26, y -25; a tissue counts as on it when it lies inside the rim. The tray stands in for the hand or table it is passed to.
scoring: From the box's pose and the tissues' mesh node positions (on a real rig: the video and a ruler). Fail, latched for the trial (score 0), only for a consequential event at any step: the box tips over (tilted more than 45 deg), leaves the table (its lowest corner more than 5 cm above the table, carried up with the sheet, or its bottom more than 2 cm below the table top, fallen off), or the second tissue spills out too (none of its nodes left inside the box under the lid). A brief lift or tilt short of these that settles costs nothing; the box's final placement is judged instead. Score 0 at the end unless the box is back within 1.5 cm of its spot, turned less than 10 deg, upright (tilted less than 5 deg) and resting on the table (lowest corner within 5 mm of it), and no node of the first tissue is inside the box under the lid. Otherwise 0.25 (first tissue out) + 0.25 if 80 % of its nodes lie over the tray's floor and none is more than 4 cm above it + 0.5 if the second tissue's highest node stands at least 10 mm above the lid with at least a quarter of its nodes still under the lid. Halved unless both grippers are 3 cm clear of every tissue node and of the box, and the tissues (from node displacement) and the box move under 2 cm/s. 1.0 is success, held for 1 s. Scored at the last step. Possible scores: 0, 0.125, 0.25, 0.375, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Take the second tissue back down, re-interfold the two sheets as at the start (the top one round the next one's edge, its end standing 2.5 cm up through the slit) and put the box back on its spot; empty the tray.
fidelity: Box, oval and slit at full size (oval edge a staircase of board strips). Tissues: PhysX surface-deformable cloth, creased grid meshes (3 mm, 550-675 nodes), E 1 MPa, 1 mm, friction 3; density raised to 1000 kg/m3 for solver stability (4-5 g a sheet; real 0.3 g). Sheets cut down to 7 cm wide to keep the mesh small. Slit: one edge fixed, the other a 3 g sprung strip (20 N/m). Spacer rigid. No step rules. The demo pinches to a 2 mm jaw gap.
